newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Sodra says postpones pulp price rise.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Sodra says postpones pulp price rise.

text.p: Swedish forestry cooperative Sodra on Tuesday said it was postponing a planned rise in pulp prices to $610 a tonne until February.
Sodra currently sells pulp at $560 a tonne and had planned to raise its prices this month.
"Our biggest competitor Weyerhauser announced earlier no change in price in Janaury," Sodra's marketing director Hans Burmeister told Reuters.
"But now many other factories have announced a lift to $610 in February instead."
Burmeister said it was difficult to analyse the current market situation.
"At the end of January the situation will be clearer," he said.
Over the Christmas weekend Swedish companies announced a cut of 10-15 percent in newsprint price but no change in pulp prices.
"This does not mean anything for pulp prices," Burmeister said.
He said making newsprint involved very little chemical pulp.
The lower newsprint prices in Sweden in 1997 were due to the lower prices overseas in 1996.
Burmeister said as newsprint price contracts are often longer it means price changes can take longer to come through.
